subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs - confirmation and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acmehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs - quick summary and asks

Hi Alicia — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

- Goal: Understand what AcmeHealth will send to Redwood in prompts and what you need back in outputs; confirm storage, retention, and residency guarantees for PII.
- Action items we covered:
  1) Which fields in prompts you consider PII (patient name, DOB, MRN, SSNs, etc.)
  2) Whether you need prompt/response logs retained for troubleshooting or audit, and for how long
  3) Data residency requirement (your workloads must remain in us-west-2)
  4) Any redaction or hashing requirements before ingesting to our runtime

From Redwood’s side, Rishi and Neha will confirm what we persist by default vs. what we can disable or shorten retention on, and outline recommended controls (redaction, on-the-fly hashing, customer-managed KMS for artifacts).

Could you confirm the list of PII fields you expect to send and whether AcmeHealth requires logs to be kept for >90 days for audits? If not, we can propose a 30-day default with an option to extend via contract.

I’ve attached a one-pager summary and the DSCP questionnaire you mentioned.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs - quick summary and asks

Hi Marissa — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from my side: 

- PII fields: patient first/last name, DOB, MRN, partial SSN, and any clinical notes that could identify a patient. We will try to minimize sensitive fields in prompts but some will be necessary for accurate outputs.
- Retention: we need logs available for up to 180 days for internal audits, but we are open to exploring a model where only hashes or redacted snippets are retained for the longer window and full-text logs are kept for 30 days.
- Residency: yes — us-west-2 only.

Can Rishi/Neha confirm whether Redwood can:
1) store full prompt/response text for 30 days,
2) then retain only hashed/metadata for up to 180 days, and
3) support customer-managed keys for any stored artifacts?

Alicia
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts/outputs - quick summary and asks

Alicia — thanks, this is clear. High-level confirmation and options from Redwood below. Please see the attached PDF for our standard config and example retention lifecycle.

What Redwood currently supports (defaults)
- Prompt and response text: persisted in our logging tier for 30 days by default to support debugging, quality monitoring, and SOC/incident investigations. Full-text logs are encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Metadata: request IDs, model version, route, timestamp, and basic request/response token counts are retained for 365 days by default.
- Residency: We can pin your tenancy to us-west-2 so all processing and storage remain in that region.

Configurable options for AcmeHealth
1) 30/180 hybrid: Keep full-text logs for 30 days (default), then expire full text and retain only hashes and minimal metadata for an additional 150 days (total 180). Hashes are one-way (SHA-256) and cannot be reversed to plaintext.
2) No full-text retention: Disable full-text prompt/response persistence entirely — only metadata and hashes retained. This reduces debugging fidelity but meets stricter privacy requirements.
3) Customer-managed keys (CMK): Support for CMKs via AWS KMS so you control key rotation and access. We will store artifacts encrypted with your key for both short-term full-text and long-term hashed artifacts.
4) Redaction helpers: Redwood can provide client-side redaction libraries and server-side pre-processing hooks to strip/replace defined PII fields before they reach persistent logs.

Notes/limitations
- If you choose to disable full-text retention, some features (end-to-end traceable debug logs, certain model-quality analytics) will be limited.
- For the hybrid model we recommend an audit log that records the retention lifecycle transitions (full-text expiry events) for compliance evidence.

Next steps
- Marissa: will capture AcmeHealth’s preferred configuration and update the deal terms (retention addendum).
- Neha: will share a short integration checklist (redaction hooks, KMS setup steps, residency confirmation doc).

If this matches your expectations we can put the 30/180 hybrid as the default in the SOW and add CMK support as an option.

Best,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra

rishi@redwood.com

Thanks Rishi — that all makes sense and matches what we were hoping for. Action items from AcmeHealth:

1) We will accept the 30/180 hybrid retention model as the default for the pilot.
2) We want CMK support for production (will request KMS key ARN and share IAM principal details).
3) We will review the redaction helper library and send a short list of fields we want redacted at the client-side.

Please go ahead and include the 30/180 addendum in the SOW draft. Once we have the KMS details I’ll coordinate with our security team for approvals.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alicia
